summary: Wallowa County, OR lookout on the Wallowa-Whitman NF: tower of disputed height dated 1933, staffed 1936-1946, removed or destroyed in the 1970s. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says removed in the 1970s; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1970s. The Forest Lookouts page's only 'Removed' label sits in its survey-mark block, not the lookout entry, so it is not used. No source describes what remains

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes a 94-foot L-6 timber tower trimmed to 72 feet in 1955; firelookout.com describes a 30-foot pole L-4 tower. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

The register says removed in the 1970s; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1970s. The Forest Lookouts 'Removed' label belongs to the NGS survey-mark record, so it is not used for the lookout. The story reports both wordings, and both agree on the 1970s.

notes_for_editor: Brief said USFS, gone, access unknown, tower; the register and firelookout.com agree on the 1933 build and the 1970s loss but disagree on tower type and height, and on removed versus destroyed. Staffing names come only from firelookout.com. The 1955 modification and the 1923 cabin note come from the register and the Forest Lookouts page respectively. The 'retired sheepman' description is the Forest Lookouts page's own narrative, not the text of the 1923 note. No source read gives access or the site's condition today. The Forest Lookouts page calls the forest the Wallowa National Forest, which is an older name; the story uses the current Wallowa-Whitman name from the register.
